issues.description: The problem statement and UML require a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon (and the template Main calls acceptSupplyDelivery), but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This name mismatch creates a structural inconsistency: students will implement acceptSupplyDelivery as specified, but the provided solution and some example code use a different method name, which may confuse tests or example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution and example code use the same method name required by the specification. Rename SealSaloon.receiveDelivery to SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity), or add a static wrapper acceptSupplyDelivery that delegates to receiveDelivery. Also ensure the template/example Main and any tests reference the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template Main call refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String,int,int) to receive ingredient deliveries, but the solution implementation provides a method named receiveDelivery(String,int,int) in SealSaloon. These two different identifiers name the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) and create a mapping confusion for students who will look for acceptSupplyDelivery in the reference implementation or whose starter Main invokes acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery(...) to acceptSupplyDelivery(...) (static) and update any internal references, or alternatively change the problem statement and template to use receiveDelivery(...). Prefer aligning the solution to acceptSupplyDelivery to match the problem description and the Main template.
